h3. Current Findings (for today).

I think I am finally getting the gist and context of the problem. I spent a lot of time today understanding the invoicing-balance systems. 

h3. admin panel

Good news: I found a way to reproduce the bug. We have to go to this admin-panel page to see it:

[https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery-courier/couriers/120700?tab=BALANCE&filter={"offset"%3A0%2C"limit"%3A25%2C"start_date_ts"%3A1727730000%2C"end_date_ts"%3A1727793000%2C"external_id"%3A120700%2C"namespace"%3Anull%2C"types"%3A["food_courier"]}&tz=Europe%2FVilnius|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery-courier/couriers/120700?tab=BALANCE&filter=%7B%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22start_date_ts%22%3A1727730000%2C%22end_date_ts%22%3A1727793000%2C%22external_id%22%3A120700%2C%22namespace%22%3Anull%2C%22types%22%3A%5B%22food_courier%22%5D%7D&tz=Europe%2FVilnius]

This happens because the admin panel gets the information from the same two sources the couriers tell on their app. The Final balance comes from the invoicing-balance service.

h3. root cause assumptions

Upon analyzing {{invoicing-delivery}} service, I discovered that the balance exporter service is the only one sending the balance transfer to the courier. Assuming we are the only ones updating the balance to couriers, this means that the root cause of the error must be in how the balance transfer is happening.

The next steps are to understand how the balance exporter service works, more specifically, how it calculates the transfers that it does. If I could find logs or traces of the values used by the balance exporter, it would be even better because then I could prove beyond doubt that the balance exporter is indeed causing the discrepancy.

Dear Marian,
Thank you for your data subject rights request, which we received on 16 September 2024.
After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 
As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties. Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.
We will share copies of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled, in particular:
* Your invoices from your previous Bolt account in London
For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our privacy notice at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides], which includes further information about:
* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.
*Your rights* 
You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 
If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the Information Commissioner’s Office and seek a judicial remedy. 
If you have any additional questions, please let us know.
Yours sincerely,
*Bolt*

Hi team, 

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer. 
You can ask the customer to reach out to their bank in order to confirm the authorized funds have been released. Their bank can locate the funds with the authorization date and amount. 


Please let me know if you have any other questions.

Cheers,
Marten

The underlying issue with JWTs for this task is the same as in [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/VULN-365?focusedCommentId=2635351|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/VULN-365?focusedCommentId=2635351|smart-link] 

We could leverage: [https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7519#autoid-14|https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7519#autoid-14|smart-link] storing {{jti}}  value of some unique identifier, ie. and in checkAuth in auth strategy check if refresh token that referenced by this unique id is still active, if not return NOT_AUTHORIZED.

However this requires modifications to common/authentication library which affects many applications globally and has to be well thought through.

TLDR; If we have identifier in the JWT that can link back to original refresh token → then we can check in API AuthStrategy for refresh token validity for given JWT. If refresh token has been revoked/expired → return NOT_AUTHORIZED response.

{noformat}SELECT session_start_path, session_starts, FTRs

group by 1
) as ftrs
ON  sessions.session_start_path = ftrs.source_page
order by 2 desc{noformat}

* Total rejection rate is 33.6%, including direct rejection and factors like no response or later-stage rejections.

** Less active drivers in the days leading up to the booking are more likely to cancel pre-booked orders.
** Using other apps could be a critical reason

adam.pantkowski: Sorry, but I can't answer this question as this is not really up to me :slightly_smiling_face: I've reached out to you, to ask whether you agree for us to implement this change.

The entire topic started internally at our team, where we realised that fraud as we know it isn't really that strictly defined. The loose definition comes from the fact that we currently have a finite set of scenarios (which are defined by the reason codes I've mentioned) that we are considering fraud, however we do not treat them equally due to the fact that some of those scenarios are handled by blocking the user (`verified_not_ok` status of a finished flow), while others are not really handled (`failed` status on finished flow) resulting in allowing the user to retry a given verification flow. That treatment however is influenced by the team/vertical that uses a given verification flow within their environment, where they define how those scenarios should be handled. Therefore, I've started to try to consolidate the behaviour by reaching out to different teams/verticals and asking whether or not those scenarios (reason codes) can be remapped, aiming at achieving a more concretely defined behaviour, i.e if a user commits fraud, they get blocked. So, in simple words, what I'm trying to change is to move from:
```user attempts to commit fraud -> user is potentially blocked, based on the type of fraud they attempt to commit```
towards
```user attempts to commit fraud -> user gets blocked ```
If those users however believe that the block was falsely applied, they can reach out to CS to get unblocked. In this case however, we enforce a human review before allowing them to proceed further, instead of simply letting them to brute force the system until succeeded.

Therefore, we would be happy to assist you and apply the change *if you give us a green light to do so*. However, if for any reason you do not want that change, we can keep the behaviour as-is.

For cases where refund was issued but can’t be seen on the user’s card or Bolt balance.

* Check where the refund was sent to and if it was successful on the [transaction history page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A%2225%22%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22target_account_id%22%3A%2265766018%22%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] 
** If Bolt balance refund is successful, there is a green button after the refund “🟢 success”
** If refund to card, 💳 success
* Check if the payment method used to make the order is not a business account. In this case, the refund will be sent to the business account balance.
* Check if the user did not spend their refund on a next order (or orders) for Bolt balance refunds
* Check if the user did not have a previous debt that was covered up with the refund
* If refund was sent to Balance instead of card, check first if payment was made from card. Usually, if card payment fails, card refund also fails. Sometimes refund will be sent to balance in cases payment was charged from balance first as debt and the refund will clear the debt previously created by the balance charge. 
* Check [payment page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments/1946767063], to ensure there are no errors on the refund and advise the user to check with their bank if card refund was successfully completed.
** If there is an error, escalate to Commerce > Ride Hailing/Food/Rentals payments
* Only successful card payments can be refunded to card.

In a nutshell:

* We round the values to precision two as we return them in the courier API. That means that when the courier app sums the value, the error propagates. The balance is calculated based on the transfers that we make (where the values are not rounded to precision 2) and, therefore, is more correct. One solution would be to modify {{billing-delivery-vat-calculator}} to send balance requests with precision two, which would fix the presentation problem but introduce error in the courier earnings. (There is a tradeoff that should be discussed between us and the billing-core team). 
* Another problem is that we only provide the records' values. The calculated value also considers the courier's initial balance. Adding the total value of the records to the initial balance can also result in error propagation, which is entirely out of our control.

Hi [~accountid:712020:9c263122-6bc1-4bbe-91d7-c80d616c4514] ,

For data accountability in insurance premium payment and insurance coverage, the insurer is mandated to request directly from the employer these basic information, even if the employee may still be providing some of this information, the responsibility lies with the employer to provide these basics. If in anyway, an error emanates from the employee that results in a wrongful data processing, they want to be sure that the payer of premium is taking responsibility by sharing the data they can base their analysis on.

The data we have agreed to share are the basics required by most insurance providers in this clime, that’s why we would not collect personal health information asides from the basic employee data. And in our employment contracts, we have mentioned that by virtue or providing some employee benefits or in relation to their employment, employees consent that we share their basic data with these providers.

Monthly coverage plan is mandatory as there are several plans with different applicable premium and as such it’s expected that the employer responsible for payment communicates the type of plan in order for the provider to charge premium accordingly. And with regards to salaries, this is also mandatory because the premium for life and disabilities insurance is dependent on how much an employee earns. And this data needs to come from the employer.

As per the data we may get from Generali, the scenario is that after the employees share their health information, an assessment is carried out to check which employee would be charged a higher premium than the standard based on the outcome of the medical assessment. As an aftermath, Generali would communicate to us basically the names of employees that may require a higher premium paid on their behalf. As an employer, we need to be aware of the potential risk of each employee as we take responsibility of the cover.

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating to Customer Payments team. The customers don't always have a great visibility when the pre-authorization has been returned to them. Returning the pre-authorization is not something Bolt has much control over. 
Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

Please leave a comment on the ticket if you still want it to be escalated to the Customer Payments team. Else the ticket will be closed in 5 days.

In order to unlock our first user stories, we need to integrate chatgpt to enable to read the chat history and the right side panel. This is what we will do first. The first user stories will be:

# When Im assigned to a new case, I want to *receive a summary* of the chat history, so that I know what I need to do.
# When I need to write a message to the user, I want to *use chatgpt prompts to improve and speed up my writing*, so that my performance and quality increases.

# This will be solely a proof of concept to explore what value it can bring to agents. We will use the feature initially only ourselves and by dedicated agents.

# When I'm assigned to a new case, I want to beehive to *suggest the correct intro message* to me, so that I don't need to write it.

* The intro itself will not be AI generated. Given the simple nature of the intro text, we can just provide a basic template in the format {{Hi {first name}, my name is {agent name} from Bolt Support}} .
* If the user does not sound stressed, there will be a template with a   at the end.
* If the case has already been handled by a previous agent, the intro will be {{Hi {first name}, my name is {agent name} from Bolt Support. I'll be taking over this case from {previous assigned agent name}.}}
* What AI needs to do in this case is to decide which template to suggest to the agent based on the chat history.

Once this is live, we have set the foundation for two things:

* AI Co-Pilot
* Templates for agents

Hello,

For cases where refund was issued but can’t be seen on the user’s card or Bolt balance.

* Check where the refund was sent to and if it was successful on the [transaction history page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A%2225%22%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22target_account_id%22%3A%2265766018%22%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] 
** If Bolt balance refund is successful, there is a green button after the refund “🟢 success”
** If refund to card, 💳 success
* Check if the payment method used to make the order is not a business account. In this case, the refund will be sent to the business account balance.
* Check if the user did not spend their refund on a next order (or orders) for Bolt balance refunds
* Check if the user did not have a previous debt or previous failed payment that was covered up with the refund
* If refund was sent to Balance instead of card, check first if payment was made from card. Usually, if card payment fails, card refund also fails. Sometimes refund will be sent to balance in cases payment was charged from balance first as debt and the refund will clear the debt previously created by the balance charge. 
* Check [payment page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments/1946767063], to ensure there are no errors on the refund and advise the user to check with their bank if card refund was successfully completed.
** If there is an error, escalate to Commerce > Ride Hailing/Food/Rentals payments
* Only successful card payments can be refunded to card.

Hello,

For cases where refund was issued but can’t be seen on the user’s card or Bolt balance.

* Check where the refund was sent to and if it was successful on the [transaction history page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A%2225%22%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22target_account_id%22%3A%2265766018%22%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] 
** If Bolt balance refund is successful, there is a green button after the refund “🟢 success”
** If refund to card, 💳 success
* Check if the payment method used to make the order is not a business account. In this case, the refund will be sent to the business account balance.
* Check if the user did not spend their refund on a next order (or orders) for Bolt balance refunds
* Check if the user did not have a previous debt or previous failed payment that was covered up with the refund
* If refund was sent to Balance instead of card, check first if payment was made from card. Usually, if card payment fails, card refund also fails. Sometimes refund will be sent to balance in cases payment was charged from balance first as debt and the refund will clear the debt previously created by the balance charge. 
* Check [payment page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments/1946767063], to ensure there are no errors on the refund and advise the user to check with their bank if card refund was successfully completed.
** If there is an error, escalate to Commerce > Ride Hailing/Food/Rentals payments
* Only successful card payments can be refunded to card.

After analysing the logs, we have the following findings:

# Only 2 orders had [the courier state race condition|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/DMO-4381] that was reported a week before on Orchestration support channel

* [https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery-order/orders/197311202|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery-order/orders/197311202]
* [https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery-order/orders/197307392|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery-order/orders/197307392]

# Due to batched orders that could not be succeeded/failed straight away, Timeouter had some latency, but it successfully finalised all of them.

# There was a lot of noise from orders created while the Timeouter was running. The orders were accepted by the provider but Timeouter considered that they should be moved to DID_NOT_RESPOND. They were self-resolved on the next successful provider state transition. Given that the provider has a generous time to accept orders, most probably the accept events were missed/ignored/overwritten

* *action item*: Investigate how provider accept events could be lost

# During the incident there were orders with instant transitions that stopped in the middle of the transition. It is already known that we do not do these instant transitions in a transaction and the [provider app should support the case when the flow was stopped in the middle|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C015U4MEKL3/p1725275314928839?thread_ts=1724327681.508369&cid=C015U4MEKL3]. In any case, there is no reason why the timeouter could not finalise this kind of order.

# Even though there were ~300 orders not finalised, the timeouter was not aware of them. There are logs where order 197311202 was the only one that timeouter was still trying to finalise.

* *action item*: Investigate how creation events could be lost. Check events retention policy

# There was the expectation that order-planner would fail the orders in 2 hours. This is not true, orders are failed by order-planner only in the case they are in a state that is waiting for a courier (ACCEPTED = waiting for the notification to start the preparation, and WAITING_PICKUP).

* *action item*: Write a document about Timeouters
* *nice to have*: Move the timeouter part of order-planner to Timeouter microservice

[*repetitive_rider_order_by_user_email*|https://github.com/bolteu/databricks-profiling-queries/blob/main/order_fraud/get_order_fraud_driver_repetitive_rider_order_by_user_email.sql] *-* only profiling query which required an exemption to postpaid businesses.

*Profiling query with postpaid exemption to test in PrestoDB* (potential databricks profiling query edit below)

{noformat}WITH count_of_orders AS (
    SELECT ot.driver_id,
           COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) AS count_of_orders,
           SUM(etl.partner_price) AS sum_of_orders
    FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
    JOIN ng_public.company_order_try ot ON etl.order_id = ot.order_id AND etl.city_id = ot.city_id
    WHERE etl.order_type = 'rides'
      AND etl.order_state = 'finished'
      AND ot.state = 'finished'
      AND etl.created >= date_add('week', -1, current_date)
      AND etl.created_date >= date_add('week', -1, current_date)
      AND ot.created >= date_add('week', -1, current_date)
      AND ot.created_date >= date_add('week', -1, current_date)
    GROUP BY 1
),
rep_orders_by_user_email AS (
         with inputs AS (
SELECT 
d.id AS calculation_id,
d.meta.order_id AS order_id,
d.meta.user_id AS user_id,
d.meta.city_id AS city_id,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.business_details.payment_type') AS method_company,
CASE WHEN json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.business_details.payment_type') = 'postpaid' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS postpaid
FROM archive_analytical.user_order_request AS d
WHERE d.created >= DATE_ADD('WEEK', -1, CURRENT_DATE)
AND d.created_hour >= DATE_ADD('WEEK', -1, CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6
)
    SELECT ot.driver_id AS driver_id,
           u.email AS user_email,
           COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) AS count_of_repetitive_rider_orders,
           COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) * 1.00 / NULLIF(coo.count_of_orders, 0) AS percentage_of_count,
           AVG(ot.distance) AS avg_pickup_distance,
           SUM(etl.partner_price_eur) AS sum_of_repetitive_rider_orders,
           SUM(etl.partner_price) * 1.00 / NULLIF(coo.sum_of_orders, 0) AS percentage_of_amount
    FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
    JOIN ng_public.company_order_try AS ot ON ot.city_id = etl.city_id AND etl.order_id = ot.order_id
    JOIN inputs AS i ON i.calculation_id = etl.fraud_calculation_id and i.postpaid = 0
    LEFT JOIN count_of_orders AS coo ON coo.driver_id = ot.driver_id
    LEFT JOIN ng_pii.user_user AS u ON u.id = etl.user_id
    WHERE etl.order_type = 'rides'
      AND etl.order_state = 'finished'
      AND etl.created >= date_add('week', -1, current_date)
      AND etl.created_date >= date_add('week', -1, current_date)
      AND ot.created >= date_add('week', -1, current_date)
      AND ot.created_date >= date_add('week', -1, current_date)
      AND ot.state = 'finished'
    GROUP BY 1, 2, coo.count_of_orders, coo.sum_of_orders
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) > 3
       AND (
           (COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) * 1.00 / NULLIF(coo.count_of_orders, 0) > 0.5) -- RULE_1
           OR (COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) * 1.00 / NULLIF(coo.count_of_orders, 0) > 0.3 AND COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) >= 4 AND AVG(ot.distance) < 500) -- RULE_2
           OR (COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) >= 8 AND AVG(ot.distance) < 1000) -- RULE_3
           OR (COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) * 1.00 / NULLIF(coo.count_of_orders, 0) > 0.3 AND SUM(etl.partner_price) * 1.00 / NULLIF(coo.sum_of_orders, 0) > 0.3 AND AVG(ot.distance) < 500) -- RULE_4
       )
)
SELECT etl.city_id,
etl.order_id,
       1 AS fraud_driver_repetitive_rider_order_by_user_email
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
JOIN ng_public.company_order_try AS ot ON ot.city_id = etl.city_id AND etl.order_id = ot.order_id
LEFT JOIN ng_pii.user_user AS u ON u.id = etl.user_id
RIGHT JOIN rep_orders_by_user_email AS ro ON ro.driver_id = ot.driver_id AND ro.user_email = u.email
LEFT JOIN ng_public.company_order AS o ON o.city_id = etl.city_id AND etl.order_id = o.id
WHERE etl.order_type = 'rides'
  AND etl.order_state = 'finished'
  AND etl.created >= date_add('week', -1, current_date)
  AND etl.created_date >= date_add('week', -1, current_date)
  AND ot.created >= date_add('week', -1, current_date)
  AND ot.created_date >= date_add('week', -1, current_date)
  AND o.created >= date_add('week', -1, current_date)
  AND o.created_date >= date_add('week', -1, current_date)
  AND ot.state = 'finished'
  AND etl.city_id NOT IN (993, 997, 991, 1167)
  AND (o.reseller_id NOT IN (9905, 752) OR o.reseller_id IS NULL)
GROUP BY 1, etl.order_id
{noformat}

As Marc said we have already activated demand netting last year [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/4379640162/Commission+Netting+-+Instructions|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/4379640162/Commission+Netting+-+Instructions|smart-link] , so conceptually this should be straightforward as supply netting already exists.

However, the blocker we have with implementing supply netting as it stands now comes from the fact that some of the branding/fleet incentives that we pay as compensations are made to companies that do not have any rides activity on the platform. This is because some fleets (usually large ones) are structured as holding companies or separate the Fleet Management activity from the actual company that operates the Fleet, and require us to split the incentive.

So we would need to find a work-aroud for these use cases as, otherwise (and as I understand) we would not be able to generate payments to these companies as long as they do not generate a positive balance.

We need to find a work-around given that:

1) We would incur additional €600-700k a year in Digital Service Tax, given that we will substantially reduce demand incentives from 2025 onwards in Spain

2) Fleet partners could churn due to the increased taxes they will suffer as this happens

Hey [~accountid:5b7bea09d08e47445d6fd01e] below my thoughts:

+*PROCESSES 1 AND 2*+

# *Ride too short block*
## the driver accepts the ride; and
## the driver then completes the ride without the passenger (we know it is fraud due to geolocation). 
# *Client did not show*
## the driver accepts the ride; and
## the driver then states it has arrived at the location and the passenger is not there (we know it is fraud due to geolocation). 

*BACKGROUND NOTES*

* these are fraud cases;
* these cases are also not in accordance with TVDE law regarding refusal of rides: 
** Article 8(1) - TVDE services may only be refused if they: a) involve circulation on roads that are clearly impassable due to difficult access or in places that pose a notorious danger to the safety of the vehicle, passengers or driver; b) are requested by people with suspiciously dangerous behaviour; c) are requested in a way that is incompatible with the provisions of this law.
* these scenarios are in accordance to t&c a reason for account suspension and termination (clauses 18.4 and 18.7)
* Blocking is a reclassification criteria and therefore communicating that there is a potential breach of the TVDE regulations can minimise the reclassification IMO. There is also a regulatory risk. In fact, Bolt as an electronic platform has the obligation to  block drivers in the case of a breach of the law: “14(2) - The operator of the electronic platform must block access to the services provided by the platform by TVDE operators, drivers or vehicles that fail to comply with any of the requirements referred to in this law, whenever it is or should be aware of this.” Failing to do so leads to a risks of fine up to 15K and license suspension up to 2 years.
* Termination will be based on a repeated behaviour. 

*GENERAL RECOMMENDATIONS*

* I suggest that the warning message makes reference to the TVDE law article Article 8(1). 
* The suspensions should follow the following principles:
** Ensure it is done in a non-discriminatory manner
*** for instance document the process and have a set of criteria applied equally
*** document the review;
*** ask for explanations during the investigation and then review
* The suspension communication shall:
** include detailed statement of reasons for the decision (i.e. include reference to the specific facts or circumstances, including contents of third party notifications, that led to the decision, as well as a reference to the applicable grounds for that decision referred in the applicable terms and conditions);
** be provided on a durable medium (that is email);
** provide the opportunity to clarify the facts and circumstances in the framework of the internal complaint-handling process by submitting a claim via the following form: [https://bolt.eu/en-mt/legal/notice/|https://bolt.eu/en-mt/legal/notice/|smart-link] .
* The termination communication shall:
** include detailed statement of reasons for the decision (i.e. include reference to the fact that there the decision is based on repeated breaches, as well as a reference to the applicable grounds for that decision referred in the applicable terms and conditions);
** be provided on a durable medium (that is email);
** provide the opportunity to clarify the facts and circumstances in the framework of the internal complaint-handling process by submitting a claim via the following form: [https://bolt.eu/en-mt/legal/notice/|https://bolt.eu/en-mt/legal/notice/|smart-link] .

*HQ ALIGNMENT*

The Legal Product team is leading a project on suspension and termination. It is therefore important to align before moving forward. This is also operational warranted because suspensions and termination require the communications to link with the internal complaint handling process, which I understand is not managed by LOPS . Hi [~accountid:619df37d657a0500708b279a] ! Please see my analysis of Estonian Employment Law below:

There is an obligation to specify the place of work in the employment contract (Article 5 (1) 8. of Estonian Employment Contracts Act.). In addition Article 20 of the same act states that an employee must perform their duties *at the employer’s place of business* which has the strongest connection with the employment relationship, unless the place of performance of work has been agreed on. *It is presumed that the place of performance of work is agreed upon with the precision of the local government (Tallinn in specific case).* This is also regulated in the BOLT TECHNOLOGY OÜ AND BOLT OPERATIONS OÜ RULES OF WORK ORGANISATION where clause 4.2.2. states that unless otherwise provided by applicable law or employment contract, an Employee shall do the work in the agreed place. Conclusion - *there is a legal obligation for Estonian employee to work at the agreed place of work which in case of Tallinn should mean Bolt offices in Tallinn.*

Clause 2.3. of the employment contract gives you the right to grant remote work permissions for your subordinate employees. Also in the new policy there will be possibility to grant such permissions in some cases (still need to wait for the full policy text but from what has been communicated, for example, in case of 2 weeks working remotely in another Bolt office in a year). Otherwise from January 1st when the new policy will be in force you as a manager will be responsible to follow it and grant such permissions according to the new policy. If the person is living in Tallinn and just prefers working from home I don’t see any reasons for fully remote work exception.

I agree that for food poisoning claims, we should request additional confirmation to avoid issuing unjustified refunds. While a doctor’s note may serve as valid proof, I see several potential challenges with this approach:

* Some customers may not feel the need to visit a doctor for mild cases, which could result in negative experiences when agents have to explain that their symptoms are not considered serious enough to qualify for a refund.

{quote}We cannot give them the contact details as that would mean a GDPR breach.{quote}

Sharing fleet contact details on an ad-hoc basis (upon request) does not violate the GDPR. If it did, then publicly displaying these details on the app would pose an even greater issue. Fleet contact details are considered business information, not personal data, and therefore is not subject to the same restrictions under GDPR and other privacy laws, which do not apply to business data.

I propose that we share fleet contact details upon request rather than making them publicly available on the app. This approach will minimize any potential risks and ensure data minimization.

The current implementation uses the {{getAccurateEtas}} cache to retrieve & set the result. 
However, caching the results as we return them will unintentionally switch to pedestrian the callers of {{getAccurateEtas}} and that’s why caching is skipped when a _switch-to-pedestrian_ happened. 
In order to fix this, caching a _switch-to-pedestrian_ should be done for the _pedestrian_ vehicle type, not the requested one. This also implies changing the retrieval strategy: for providers that are <200m away, two keys should be used: one for vehicle_type and one for pedestrian. If both of them have values, the one with the smaller duration will be preferred.
Another issue with caching can happen when {{getApproximateEtas}} retrieves results cached by {{getAccurateEtas}}: these results should also be switched to pedestrian (if necessary).
This requires some more serious refactoring and will be tackled in a separate task.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*General comments and questions*
{panel}

* What kinds of questions are we receiving? Could you give some examples?
* Where have we taken these requirements from? Generally, they do not seem to be consistent with our process and they do not reflect our legal position. I will propose alternative wording below. 

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Regarding CCTV*
{panel}

We have a Beehive KB article (available here: [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/33697?country=global&language=en|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/33697?country=global&language=en]) that reflects our position.

To summarize what is stated in this BH KB article:

* First and foremost - Bolt and drivers are two independent parties when it comes to use of personal data. In other words - we act as independent data controllers, where neither party can give instructions to the other party on how the data can be used (or how any obligations under the GDPR have to be met). The drivers decide on that for themselves and they bear the responsibility for non-compliance.
* We can advise the driver to have a CCTV sign to comply with transparency requirements they have. However, we should not be giving directions, and the current wording uses words like “you need to” which looks like an instruction to the drivers.
* We can advise the driver to provide information on where customers can access a comprehensive CCTV privacy notice.
* We can explain that the above will help inform customers about how their data is being used.
* However, we need to stay consistent with our position and acknowledge that while these are recommendations, the driver has the autonomy to decide whether to follow them.
* Based on the above, we can’t use the wording proposed.



 *I suggest adjusting the message to the following to match the BH KB article:*



{quote}_Hi,_

_If you use CCTV cameras, we recommend that you ensure that you have the CCTV warning sign and enhance it by providing key details such as the purpose of the CCTV, the controller's name, the data retention period, and information on where customers can access a comprehensive CCTV privacy notice. This will help ensure transparency and compliance with privacy regulations._

_We encourage you to review your Privacy Notices and ensure that it outlines how personal data from CCTV is processed._ 

_Kindly ensure that you inform customers about the processing of their personal data and CCTV records._

_Please be aware that non-compliance with these requirements could potentially lead to legal consequences due to breaches of privacy laws._

_While we offer these recommendations, we want to emphasize that as independent data controllers, you have the autonomy to decide whether to follow our advice. However, it's important to note that you are accountable for any violations._{quote}

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Regarding Audio Trip Recording*
{panel}

* Generally, the wording needs to be consistent with the position above - we can’t force or instruct the drivers to do anything when it comes to data use.
* We should stay within the lines of what we communicate in-app and publicly on our website, i.e. [https://bolt.eu/en/blog/audio-trip-recording-feature/|https://bolt.eu/en/blog/audio-trip-recording-feature/|smart-link] .
* I strongly suggest removing any references to the obligation to have a sticker. Can you let me know where it comes from and whether this is something that we encourage the drivers to do?

 *I suggest adjusting the message to the following:*

{quote}_Hi. Regarding audio recording in the Bolt app - both the driver and passenger have the option to start audio recording during the ride at any time. Recording must be initiated by the user, it does not happen automatically when the ride starts. The audio files with the audio recording of the ride are encrypted, so neither the driver nor the passenger can listen to them. This can only be done by the Bolt Safety Team if an audio file is given to the Support Team with a description of the case. If no security incident is reported within 24 hours, the recording file will automatically delete itself from the device._{quote}

Hey [~accountid:712020:13033e65-435c-4794-a380-e007eba7615a] , see my thoughts below:



* Romania has specific legislation regarding taxes, and we have been actively lobbying and discussing with the Licensing Authority about how the new law should be structured. The ticket that Sorina linked below is about it.

* *Regarding this specific request:*
** We should inform the team that we are able to disclose the requested data.
** I agree with Sorina's proposal to mention that we are disclosing the data based on the law she referenced.
*** We should kindly ask the requesting authority to cite the correct law in their future requests.



{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*General approach to handling such requests*
{panel}

* *Volume of data doesn’t equate to excessiveness*
** A large number of rows in an Excel sheet does not necessarily mean the request is excessive or disproportionate.
** In this Romanian case, the authority has clearly stated they are investigating a specific fleet.
* *What we need to aim for is understanding the purpose of the investigation:*
** When authorities (fiscal, tax, social security, etc.) are investigating a fleet for purposes like tax evasion or licensing compliance, it is natural for them to request data on the drivers associated with that fleet.
*** Limiting the number of drivers' data provided may not make sense, as it might not be consistent with the investigation’s purpose.
* *Focus on data types rather than quantity:*
** It's important to consider what specific data the authority needs rather than the number of data subjects involved.
* *Challenging the scope when appropriate:*
** If the police are requesting data for a one-off crime (e.g., murder) rather than a continuous crime (e.g., tax evasion), we may have grounds to challenge the scope of the request.
* *Being pragmatic with licensing authorities*
** Being pragmatic with licensing authorities is crucial, as non-disclosure of data might affect our license in a specific market.
*** In Romania, we've recently renewed our license and have faced significant media attention due to the phishing/P1 incident.
*** We must ensure we're not jeopardizing our license by resisting legitimate LERs in this region.
* *Assessing the risk to data subjects:*
** When handling LERs, consider whether disclosing the data poses a real risk to the data subjects.
*** For example, providing 1500 driver names and contact details to an authority investigating a sensitive crime like rape could cause stress/discomfort if they contact the drivers.
*** In contrast, sharing driver names and earnings with authorities investigating tax evasion within a fleet presents a low risk to the users.

Hello! 🐸 long answer alert 

After investigating the issue with dots and Gmail, I discovered that [+honeybadger@gmail.com+|mailto:honeybadger@gmail.com] and [+honey.badger@gmail.com+|mailto:honey.badger@gmail.com] can’t belong to two different people.

If person A registers with a [+honeybadger@gmail.com+|mailto:honeybadger@gmail.com] Gmail, then automatically all the “dotted” versions of that email will belong to person A. This means that if person B decides to register on Gmail with [+honey.badger@gmail.com+|mailto:honey.badger@gmail.com], Google will not allow them to do it, and it will tell them that this email is already registered by someone else (person A).

That’s why if person A is not registered at Bolt but receives person B’s receipts on their email, it means that person B mentioned person A’s email when they were registering at Bolt, which is incorrect. For example, person B’s email was [honey.badger88@gmail.com|mailto:honeybadger88@gmail.com], but they registered at Bolt with [honey.badger@gmail.com|mailto:honey.badger@gmail.com], this means that they mentioned an incorrect email (person A’s).

Now, when it comes to the tickets that you guys shared:

* [Link 1|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/453834721] - when I search for the email I can see [{color:#0747a6}this Rider account{color}|https://admin.bolt.eu/user/Users/user/21886908] that is registered with it. [{color:#0747a6}This is the order{color}|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/1244251772/374?orderTryId=1769195737] they got the receipt for. * [Link 2|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/454127522] - here if I search for [jadranka.ilic@gmail.com|mailto:jadranka.ilic@gmail.com], there are no accounts in Admin. But if I remove the dot and search for [jadrankailic@gmail.com|mailto:jadranka.ilic@gmail.com], I see [this Rider account|https://admin.bolt.eu/user/users/user/232623141], and [{color:#0747a6}this is the order{color}|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/1244514105/374?orderTryId=1770029293] that they got the receipt for. Again, the agent needs to follow the wrong email process in KB to resolve the stuation.

Hello, we should under no circumstances ask for a doctor’s note from the clients as proof of a food poisoning:

* Firstly, doctor’s notes are a medical record and clients are not obligated to share this personal data;
* Secondly, our systems and tools (Beehive, Admin, Cognito) are not meant for the storage of such medical documents (where would we safely store this document should we receive it?);
* Finally, from the Risk team’s perspective on the investigation flow, we do not see how it would help along with the investigation as the food poisoning could’ve come from anywhere (meaning not from the food that was distributed through our app). It’s basically a he-said-she-said situation, meaning we should mainly take a look at the history of the user and provider and make our final decision based on that, including the severity of the current report. 

What we could do:

* Stop issuing refunds for clients who report multiple food poisonings over a short period of time.
** I would not advise to stop refunding completely, as food poisoning itself is already a very bad experience which affects a client physically. If we then refuse to refund, it may start escalating further on (social) media.
* Determine ‘markers’ for profiles which are likely fraudulent to help agents with the final decision - maybe we already have something like this that we could transfer over from Rides vertical?
* Account Managers/Merchant Operations teams should start contacting providers if we have multiple food poisoning reports in order to pass on the complaint, so the provider could conduct their own internal investigation where needed.

We have put together a looker dashboard where we can see [*recurring Delivery safety events*|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/dashboards/20590?Count+Events=%3E%3D3&Country=Poland&Courier+ID+%5BDrill+Down%5D=&Eater+ID+%5BDrill+Down%5D=&Event+Date=&Provider+ID+%5BDrill+Down%5D=] per country and user type, which should assist our internal teams with looking into those repetitive reports.

Let me know if any questions 🙏

* Regarding using AMEX cards in Euro Zone - turns out the info on KB is incorrect. The user will be able to add the American Express card successfully anywhere in the world, but they might face some issues with paying for the services based on their bank issues/acquirer. 
** The payments team does not care about the phone numbers that the customer uses to sign up.
** Locations in Bolt are determined by the user's GPS location. Each country has different payment methods based on the GPS location and customers can only see available payment methods in their country.
For example, you add a card payment method in Estonia, but when you go to Angola (only cash payment method available), then you will not be able to see the card method anymore even though it is saved to your profile.
* Regarding FRAUD_RISK_BLOCK error - this temporary error occurs when someone makes too many attempts to add a new card within a short timeframe. The best is for CS to raise the SD ticket with the Fraud team and wait for their input.

Based on the info above:

* I’ll remove the *_American Express cards are only accepted in Euro Zone countries and in South Africa_* sentence from the article;
* I’ll add the FRAUD_RISK_BLOCK error with an explanation and instructions to the *Fraud errors* section of the article. 

Once the changes reflect on KB, I’ll share a post about it in the Slack updates channel.

Hi! Our approach for data validation / sanitization is next: we are doing sanitization _before using_, not _before saving_. 

And here are the reasons why pre-saving sanitization is not perfect:

* For different output channel we might need different escape strategy (e.g. escape {{"}} for SQL and escape {{< >}} for HTML). Trying to apply all of them at once before saving might corrupt the data.
* In case we update sanitization logic, new rules will be applied only to the new values. Applying new rules for already stored data is very complicated.

We could deny {{<}} and {{>}} in "First Name” field to solve this particular HTMLi vulnerability. But we can't disable it for all fields by default, because in some fields it might be a valid input (formulas, email address etc).

More efficient approach is sanitization on-the-fly directly before usage. At this moment we know which channel will be used (sql, email, sms, website etc). And we can apply escaping which is required for this particular channel.



To address this specific issue with discovered *HTMLi* vulnerability, I suggest that we add proper sanitization before sending:

# *Sending emails from our backend.* It is done via email service, owned by *comms* team. Let’s ask them in *#dev-comms-support* Slack.
## It makes sense to escape HTML in all template variables. If some of them require raw HTML input, the syntax for these variables should be different. Like {{[$name]}} for regular variables and {{[unsafe_html$var]}} for variables that need markup.
## Also makes sense to check logic how value of “To: “ field is composed, because it could be like {{To: First Name <somemail@gmail.com>}} and also could be compromised by {{first_name}} value.
# *Sending emails from LCM*. Current flow is next: {{product code}} → {{event micro service}} → {{RudderStack}} → {{Braze}}. Two in the middle are owned by MarTech team. We can reach out to them in *#dev-martech-support ,* Braze is owned by *#lifecycle-support*. 
## Sanitization could be done on the RudderStack for the Braze destination using {{transform}} script. 
### Pros: it will remain if we change tool (Braze → CleverTap or something else)
### Cons: it does not distinguish SMS from Email and from push notification (for SMS we might need different escape than for email)
#### *UPD:* if we start applying it via Rudderstack - it will help only with new values. But it will give enough protection because usually attacks require fresh attempts.
## If the first option will be rejected, we can do sanitization on the Braze side, because here we can distinguish between email, SMS and Push Notification channels and apply relevant sanitization.



PS: Let’s not disclose details of the vulnerability in the public channels.

Hi [~accountid:712020:0bd2fbbd-2638-4a3c-a746-72ee1e38d570] ,

* It is considered that *hard opt-in* *(explicit consent) is required* in Poland for any kind of direct marketing/outbound sales activities, *therefore Bolt should not be engaged into cold mailing without obtaining such consent*.
* However, understanding that resignation from cold mailing might have a huge business impact on Bolt, there are some actions that *might improve* (but will not exclude any risk) our situation in case of any problems: 
** Asking for a consent to be provided with Bolt’s offer without presenting details in the initial e-mail  - {color:#ffc400}*medium risk*{color}
** Sending offers to business e-mails that can reasonable be considered as address to which marketing correspondence can be sent (e.g. [sprzedaz@xx.com|mailto:sprzedaz@xx.com], [sales@xx.com|mailto:sales@xx.com], etc.) - {color:#ffc400}*medium risk*{color}
** Sending offers to partner’s employees whose positions are related to sales, marketing, etc. - {color:#ff5630}*high risk*{color}
* On *10 November 2024* a new act governing this matter will be in force (Electronic Communication Act (the *“ECA*”)), therefore interpretations of the current law may soon be outdated.
* It is already commented by legal professionals that cold e-mails will not be allowed under the ECA ([Example|https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/prawo-komunikacji-elektronicznej-jakie-zmiany-w-pawe%C5%82-litwi%C5%84ski-mruaf?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_android&utm_campaign=share_via]). Yet they disagree with such approach of the authorities.
* *Polish authorities are very strict as to the issue of consent for direct marketing*. There is even a position that contacting the end-user to obtain his/her consent should be considered as a direct marketing activity which generally means that you are not allowed to offer any products of services if you have not obtained prior consent in any other way). On the other hand, *Polish courts usually present slightly less strict position* and - in this specific case (judgment of the Warsaw-Praga Regional Court of 4 January 2019, IV Ca 1873/16) - even allowed to contact a consumer to obtain his/her consent for direct marketing.
* *In the case of failure to comply with the obligation to obtain the end-user consent the President of UKE shall, by decision, impose on the entity, taking into account the nature and scope of the violation, a fine of up to 3% of the fined entity's revenue earned in the previous calendar year or up to PLN 1,000,000, with the higher amount applying.* 
* Non-compliance with the above obligation may also constitute an act of unfair competition within the meaning of the provisions of the Act on Combating Unfair Competition of April 16, 1993 (Journal of Laws of 2022, item 1233).
* The above relates to the consent that has to be obtained based on the ECA act. It is considered that under GDPR (_RODO_) there is no additional consent required.

*I consider contacting other people with Bolt’s offer as risky (unless Bolt receives prior consent for marketing contacts)*, *therefore any cold emailing shall be made only after consideration of the above risks.*

Hello [~accountid:60d6dd5bf6505400698b38f9],

The issue is that this is a Business Company account, where a business reports it’s taxes from the account to the tax authority.

This account belongs to a business, only one business, and there can be no activity for another business. 

Changing the name or the address of this business is OK, assuming it’s the same business, as this happens in real life. 

Changing the VAT code is not acceptable, as company’s do not change VAT codes, so in this case it means we are talking about a different company.

The above applies to a Business Company account and differs from a Work Profile, where it is OK to change the name and VAT code, in most circumstances.

Hey! The police came back with the following legal basis:

As further support that a release of requested personal data can take place, Article 6.1 f of the Data Protection Regulation is stated - if it is necessary for purposes relating to the legitimate interests of the personal data controller or a third party, unless the interests and fundamental rights and freedoms of the data subject outweigh and require protection of personal data.

We at the Police Authority have a very strong legitimate interest in processing personal data to fight crime. Even if there is no constitutional obligation to provide information or it would be incompatible with the collection purposes to disclose information to the police, disclosure should generally be permitted after a balance of interests in the individual case. When balancing interests, it must therefore always be taken into account that the Police Authority's mission to fight crime is a constitutionally regulated and important public interest. The police authority is responsible for only requesting information when there is a concrete need and legal prerequisites for processing by the authority. The private actor can therefore always assume in its balancing of interests that the Police Authority has a strong legitimate interest in accessing the requested information, even if the authority cannot explain the background to the request in the individual case for reasons of confidentiality.

All tasks that the Riksdag or the government have assigned to state authorities to perform are of public interest, as is evident from the preparatory work for the new Swedish data protection regulation. When balancing interests, it should also be taken into account, as stated above, that the data is normally protected by the Police Authority. Against this background, a balancing of interests in accordance with Article 6.1 f of the data protection regulation must generally mean that a company may disclose requested personal data, now that these are requested in the law enforcement activities of the police. # As the guidelines you linked mentioned, when it comes to lotteries/raffles, then there is a risk that the raffle can be considered “gambling” under local laws and additional requirements apply / it’s forbidden under local laws. Here is an [overview of the regulations |https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/5133303809/Country+specific+rules+on+games+of+chance]for each market - although this guideline focuses on consumers (eaters), it’s safe to assume that the risk level is similar for couriers as well:

* EE, LT, LV, CZ, SK, KE, AZ, UA - low risk, I just need to prepare TCs
* GH, HR - medium risk, I will need to get approval from local counsel.
* PL, RO, MT, PT - high risk, not advisable to run these campaigns there.

# When it comes to reclassification, the “do X amount of deliveries within Y amount of time” style campaigns are less risky, as long as the “Y amount of time” is not so unreasonably short that the courier would have to stay online for e.g. 10 hours straight each day to be able to realistically achieve the goal. That said, currently PT and MT are the “riskier” markets from reclass side where I would not advise to run this campaign - but they are also risky from the “lottery regulations” side (point 1 above).

I have checked the case and confirm that everything looks fine on Bolt’s end. 

There are a couple of nuances with the payment that can cause some confusion. 
The ride fare and the tip are processed as one transaction. 21.09 PLN was charged from the customer (18.09 + 3)

In Poland we are using incremental authorization. 
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change. 

We have initially authorized 18.09 PLN and then 3 PLN. This is why the customer sees the authorizations as different charges. 
The authorizations have been released to the customer. 
The customer can confirm with their bank the funds have been returned. Their bank should be able to locate the payment with the authorization date and amount. You can also provide the Acquirer reference {{429319150029}}.

The 🚨🚗 [Rides Safety case handling workflow for Low/moderate events|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/47156?country=global&language=en] article’s *_Handling counterclaims for Low and Moderate events_* section states that: 

{quote}* Resolve the counterclaim by following the applicable safety process depending on the severity of the case. Check the [🚨🚗 List of Ride-hailing Safety Events|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4402562822930000].
** If the counterclaim is of *High* or *Significant* severity, escalate the case to the Safety team by choosing the applicable severity level.{quote}

So, if the initial safety report is of low/moderate severity, but there is a high/significant severity counterclaim, it should be escalated to the Safety team to handle, as the counterclaim should be perceived as a new safety report. 

When it comes to the counterclaim note, if the initial report is of low/moderate severity and is from a market where the Global Event Assessment tool isn’t used for logging events, then the applicable note would be the one without the tool reference number: 

{quote}COUNTERCLAIM
[Enter Event Category]:
[Enter any additional Event Categories reported]:
Reporting party Ticket:
Reported party Ticket:{quote}

This specific template is applicable in the situation you described because the initial report does not have a tool reference number you can include in the note since no tool is logged for low/moderate cases _(depending on the market)_. 

If you work in a market that does not use the Global Event Assessment tool for low/moderate cases, you can find all applicable and relevant additional information, including the applicable internal note/Admin comment templates, in the 🚨🚗 [Safety: guidelines for Low/moderate events|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/50085?country=global&language=en] article.

Dear Florian,

Thank you for your data subject rights request, which we received on 21 September 2024.

We take your privacy seriously. As a part of this commitment, we would like to clarify Bolt’s practices in relation to collecting and processing your location information.

Bolt may use your geolocation data for various purposes, including to suggest new rides and destinations depending on the consents you have provided in your Bolt app. You can always disable these specific notifications, without disabling all Bolt notifications. Further information in this regard can be found in our privacy notice available at [https://bolt.eu/de-de/privacy/privacy-for-riders/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/de-de/privacy/privacy-for-riders/?category=rides].

Additionally, please note the following:

* Bolt starts collecting your location data when you grant permission to tracking it for either ‘All time', ‘While using the App’ or ‘Once’. Bolt asks for such permission on sign in; however, such permission can be revoked or granted at any time via your device settings (either when a prompt to authorise background use is displayed in the Bolt app or on your own). Your location information is collected only in the foreground. This means that Bolt starts collecting your location data when you open the Bolt app and stops collecting it when you close the Bolt app.
* The permission to share your location data ‘All the time’ applies only to the geofencing feature, which is used to notify you if Bolt is operating in a specific geographic area. Bolt does not, however, store any of your location data in relation to this. iOS and Android devices enable apps to automatically trigger notifications when the user enters a specific geographic area. This does not require the Bolt app to run in the background or mobile data to be used. Apple and Android store this information at their end and automatically trigger those notifications when a user enters a defined geographic area, without sharing the user’s location with Bolt.

*Your rights* 

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt*

*How to calculate and select the breather valve*:

Valve supplier: [https://www.en.suyang-tech.com/prdocuts/1141751763348860928-6-6.html|https://www.en.suyang-tech.com/prdocuts/1141751763348860928-6-6.html|smart-link] 

|According to the temperature shock requirements of 8.2.8 of the national standard "GB/T 38031-2020", the battery pack should be placed in an alternating environment of -40 ° C ±2 ° C to 60 ° C ±2 ° C, and the conversion time between the two extreme temperatures should be within 30 minutes. 
If the net volume of air in the battery pack is V0, and the temperature of the battery pack rises from -40 ° C to 60 ° C, the amount of gas expansion is the breathable amount of the explosion-proof valve. According to the Charlie-Gay-Lussac law, when the pressure is constant, the volume of a certain mass of gas is proportional to the thermodynamic temperature, which can be obtained:
V1/V0=T1/T0，公式（1）
Q=(V1-V0)/t×1.5，公式（2）|
|* V0 is the air volume of the battery pack
* V1 is the gas volume of the battery pack at 60 ° C
* T0 is the initial temperature of the battery pack (-40+273 K)
* T1 is the maximum temperature of the battery pack (60+273 K)
* t is the temperature rise time (that is, the time required for exhaust 30min)
* 1.5 is the safety factor (considered according to the actual situation).
Q is the required air permeability, and select valve which is getting air permeability higher than required from datasheet.|



|*C3 battery data:*
* Total volume of the casing: 1.87L
* Core pack volume: 1.13L
* Free air volume in the battery after assembly: 1.87-1.13 = 0.74L (nominal volume on temperature 22 degrees)

*Temperature range:*
Tmin: -40 degrees
Tmax: 60 degrees
safety factor: 1.5

Q0 = 592ml (-40 degrees)
Q1 = 846ml (60 degrees)
ΔQ = 254 ml (total volume that we have to ventilate in case the temperature change from -40 to +60 C)

Q=(846-592)/30*1.5 = 12.75 ml/min
Based on standard the ventilation time/period is 30 min.|

~ Investigation ~

~ *I. Summary of the events* ~

The driver chaotically (in several separate Beehive communications) informed us that his account has been hacked. The following summary points out the most important issues found during the investigation (most of the communication is repetititve):

a) [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/449766709|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/449766709] - The driver knew what phone was used by an unidentified user - “Please can you log me out of that A02 please”.

Additionally, the alleged driver started sending the pictures from social media of the person with unauthorised access. 

b) [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/450318532|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/450318532] - The person admits that the unauthorised individual was helping him with changing details on his account - “Yes he was helping me wth the car. And he changed my number to his number”

c) This has been confirmed in the first communication - [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/449766709|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/449766709] - “There was a guy who helped me upload my car im sure he is the one who changed it”. 

*~ II. Short summary of the most crucial parts ~*

The driver claims that his account has been hacked. In the communication on Beehive, however, he admits to have been using help from an unauthorised individual to implement changes on his profile. 

Precautionary measures were taken to safeguard the account. The phone number and email address linked to the account were reverted to their original state. 

~ *III. Questions to be answered* ~

# *What data was accessed?*

Presumably, the fraudster had access to the account.

# *How the account was accessed - was it a malfunction of our systems or processes, or was it the user’s actions that caused it?*

It is not confirmed how the account was accessed. There is no evidence to suggest a malfunction of the systems or processes. The user suggested that someone they know might have accessed their account by sending pictures of a different individual. The alleged driver also claimed that this individual was helping him with the account’s set-up. This implies that the access may have been due to the user’s actions or circumstances involving someone they know, rather than a system failure.

# *Has the user suffered any harm/loss (e.g. financial loss, data has been leaked, etc.)*

Reportedly, the user did not suffer any financial loss. As for now, there is no indication that any data was leaked or that the user suffered other forms of harm.

# *What mitigation steps have been undertaken?*

To be confirmed. 

~ *III. Admin’s Portal investigation* ~

a. Between the 26th September and and 6th of October, there have been four different devices have been logged in into a device. It seems that only one device, which logged in for the first time on the 14th of August 2024, still has the access to the account.

b. Passed selfie-verifications, all from the car’s interior.  

*~ IV. Proposed Actions and Conclusions ~*

It seems that the driver has voluntarily given up the access to his account. We simply need to record the breach in our Cognito form - making it clear that this was a an unauthorised access facilitated by the Driver and that it was promptly resolved by CS following our procedures.

*What is the internal process in Bolt to ensure the vehicles are operational before a user initiates a ride?*

* Deployment Inspection: Vehicles undergo a thorough inspection in the warehouse before being put on the street to ensure they meet safety standards.

* Client feedback: If a user reports a problem, it is flagged in Bolt's system for immediate attention.

* On 19 October, [driver|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fleet/drivers/edit/2311523?tab=profile&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] wrote to Bolt CS with the message “_Urgent: Breach of GDPR Regulations and Platform Trust_”. In particular, they have specified the following:
** “_I have been made aware that my messages, shared via the Bolt platform, have been passed by Bolt employees to external messaging applications… The purpose of my comments regarding passenger behavior has been to help both Bolt and the passenger understand the reasons for any negative rating_”.
* We requested the source of this information / screenshots. 
** Unfortunately, CS made this request on the basis that “_we do not share personal information_”, which is not strictly correct.
* Driver responded “_As a partner, I am under no obligation to provide you with the sources of my information or screenshots. I have raised this issue in good faith_”
* CS internal investigation showed the following:
** “_I investigated his reports and didn't locate tickets of agents sharing sensitive details with riders, agents shared only date of the reported ride and asking what happened or educated rider about damaged vehicle/underage passenger_”
** “_On driver profile, I noticed that driver is sharing with us feedbacks from the rides, but there wasn't anything suspicious and agents didn't share sensitive details with rider. However, I am not able to find reported incident outside of the platform without more information from driver._”

+*THOUGHTS*+

* Based on my own investigation of the driver’s profile:
** Driver has in the past (on multiple occasions) written to Bolt commenting on rationale behind cancelling certain trips (see [here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/457752734]) or to complain about an underage passenger using the platform (see [here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/450832882] and [here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/452959806]). ** There are even Beehive tickets (e.g., [here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/423117402]) where the driver calls CS to inform them that he is logging on…
** The driver has noted in multiple chats that they are saving all data that they collect should any legal action be necessary. They have not directly threatened legal action yet, but they are hovering the concept over our heads.
** In a Beehive ticket, the user has noted that they are “_an official Data Protection Officer registered with the Information Commissioner’s Office_”. He is not immediately obvious from a quick Google.
** In short, this individual seems to be a privacy-conscious ‘rights warrior’ who seems to have a bone to pick with Bolt. We should try to de-escalate this as much as possible - however, it is likely that any response we provide may ben met in a similarly combative manner.
* Having reviewed the profile / tickets, it is not obvious what the driver is concerned about. ** What messages of theirs were allegedly shared.
** Which third parties the messages have been allegedly shared with.
** How they became aware of this issue.

Hi all, 

*“Reward”* is ok. Should be the word to use.

*“Cashback”* I understand its suggested not to use this word. I am not sure where it comes from. However, I have made additional research and looks like as long as the cashback campaign aligns with the described structure (made available to your Bolt Balance account and not withdrawable/refundable as cash), it is fine to use the term “cashback”.  

*“Bonus”* I see its agreed not to use it for Partners. 
For customers. Bonus is a term commonly used in gambling and gaming (regulated industry) marketing campaigns so it might sound a bit alarming, but it is not exclusive to those industries. If you have clear communications and terms to avoid confusion, it should be fine, but I agree with your approach.  

*“credit”* is not ok. The definition of credit first varies depending on the country and second implies a repayment of the credit to the creditor. Lets do not say we “credit” amounts to you, but we make them available to you. We should not use this word at all. Keep in mind we try to stay away from anything that may suggest or be interpreted as we have a financial license.    

[From Bolt Balance Terms|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/bolt-balance-terms/?category=rides]: Bolt Balance displays amounts which you can use for purchases of goods and services available on the Bolt app. Such amounts may be available to you because: (a) you have withdrawn from the purchase of any of the goods or services purchased using the Bolt app and the *amounts you paid have been returned to you by way of making these amounts available to you on Bolt Balance*; (b) you have had a negative experience using the Bolt app and these amounts have been made available to you as *compensation* thereof; (*c) these amounts have been made available to you as part of a promotional campaign or otherwise just because we wanted to;* (d) you have used the Top-Up Function;

I recommend to align the wording and terms used for all campaigns involving Bolt Balance with Bolt Balance T&Cs. 

If you have any questions please let me know.

Hi All, 

I confirm that from a legal POV, we can share requested information with the bailiff. 

The basis is article 660 of the Civil Procedure Code which has the wording as follows (translated from RO to ENG):

{quote}_Duty of third parties to provide information_
_(1)_ *_At the request of the bailiff_*_, those who owe sums of money to the debtor being pursued or who hold assets of the debtor subject to pursuit, according to the law,_ *_shall have the duty to communicate in writing all information necessary for the execution. They are required to declare the extent of their obligations towards the debtor being pursued, any arrangements that could affect them, previous seizures, assignments of claims, subrogations, debt assumption, novations, and any other acts or facts likely to alter the content or the parties to the obligation relationship or the legal status of the property held_*_. At the request of the bailiff or of the interested party, the executing court may take the measures referred to in Article 187 paragraph. (1) point 2 f) and Article 189._
_(2) Furthermore, at the request of the bailiff, public institutions, credit institutions and any other natural or_ *_legal persons shall be obliged to immediately communicate to the bailiff, in copy, the documents and, in writing, the data and information deemed by the bailiff as necessary for the enforcement of the execution, including the personal identification number of the person subject to the enforcement, even if otherwise provided for by special laws_*_.Similarly, the tax authorities shall be obliged to communicate, under the same conditions, the data and information they administer according to the law. At the request of the bailiff or of the interested party, the enforcement court may take the measures provided for in Article 187 para. (1) point 2 f) and Article 189._
_(3) If the information requested is not available to the parties notified or, as the case may be, they refuse to provide it, the Public Ministry shall, at the request of the bailiff, take the necessary steps to obtain the information requested, in particular to identify the public or private entities with which the debtor has opened bank accounts or deposits, has investments in securities, is a shareholder or partner or, as the case may be, holds government securities, treasury bills and other securities subject to levy of execution._
_(4) The bailiff shall be bound to maintain the secrecy of the information received, unless otherwise provided by law. This information may only be used for the purpose for which it was requested, and its disclosure to third parties or its use for the creation of a personal database is strictly prohibited, under the penalties provided by law._
_(5) In order to obtain the information necessary for the enforcement, the bailiff shall have free access to the land register, the commercial register and other public registers containing data on the debtor's assets subject to levy of execution. At the same time, the bailiff may request from the executing court the data and information referred to in Article 154 paragraph. (8)._{quote}

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *8 September 2024.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.



We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order History (Pick-up and Drop-off)*



For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|smart-link] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.





Yours sincerely,



Bolt
