APP fraud (authorised push payments fraud) - victim willingly transfers money to the fraudster. Normal course of action is to report this to police, but rarely they can catch criminals and retrieve the money. Banks are unhelpful, because since it was authorised transaction they cannot do anything about it. Some banks recently started offering protection from APP fraud,  i.e. they would cover victim's losses, we may double check it with our bank, but it is rare practice and unlikely that we will be covered.

In this situation it is unlikely that we can recover money that we transferred and unless we will blame the Partner for unauthorised access we will still be under the obligation to transfer money to the Partner.

First steps now:

# Contact bank providing details of payments, such as the recipient's account information, date, and amount of the transaction. Ask bank to recall the funds. They will probably refuse, because it was authorised transaction, but it is worth trying.
# Report fraud to the Police.
# Decide how we want to proceed in relation to the Partner. Since Partners did not receive funds that fraudsters stole, they may argue that Bolt still owes them money.
## It is likely that we are able using provisions of the agreement we have with the Partner say that we acted in accordance with their instructions and that we don’t have obligation to reconfirm their instructions before we act upon them. Therefore, we may say that we are discharged from our obligation to pay them the money that was transferred to the fraudsters as we already made payments in accordance with their instructions, even if instructions were given not by the Partner itself. If this is the route we want to take, then we will need to: 1) check with our IT people whether there were any problems on our system’s side that enabled fraudsters to contact us (in case it is a weakness in our system rather than Partner sharing their credentials with fraudsters); 2) I will need to see agreements that we have with the Partners (Special Terms) and prepare appropriate response. 
This approach may damage relationship between us and Partners.
## If we decide to take the hit and reimburse Partners, then we still need to notify them about what has happened and reassure them that they will receive their money.

+*SUMMARY*+

* UK rider claims their account was hacked, they suffered £600 in detriment, and their account was subsequently erased.
** In reality, the account has not been erased - just taken over by a hacker. 
** However, I am confident that compromise has taken place here, and that the user has suffered financial detriment (does not appear to be ongoing). As such, this seems to be a reportable personal data breach.
* UK rider has framed the following as data subject rights requests:
** 18 Sept: “_I need to recover_ [my account]”
** 19 Oct: “_I need a confirmation from your part that I have been scammed and my Bolt app has been hacked_”
{panel}

*FULL BACKGROUND*

* On 18 September, the phone number on [this account|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/77075493/overview?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] (“*Account 1*”) was changed (from +447960182471 (the “*Real Phone Number*”) to +447300504175 (the “*Fake Phone Number*”)). No other details changed.
** A block was introduced on 18 September ('Number of recently rejected order requests was more than allowed'), but this block was subsequently removed. Account 1 is still active.
** There are five active [payment methods|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/users/67870145?tab=instruments] on the account from before the period of compromise. One of these methods ends in 0618 and expires 04/27 (the “*Payment Method*”)
** 28 [order attempts|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A50%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22start_timestamp%22%3A1718997480%2C%22end_timestamp%22%3A1729551599.999%2C%22all_order_try_states%22%3Afalse%2C%22user_id%22%3A77075493%7D%7D&source_id=&city_id=&user_id=] were then made in the space of a number of hours. Many of these were marked as fraudulent. No trips have been taken since. All of the [payments|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments?userId=77075493&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22userType%22%3A%22user%22%2C%22from%22%3A1713657600.543%2C%22to%22%3A1729555199.543%2C%22userId%22%3A77075493%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] are marked as either ‘Failed’ 'Chargedback’ or ’Cancelled'. The majority were done via the Payment Method, with the exception of two other payment methods also already on Account 1.
** Four new devices were logged on the same day. These were all deactivated / signed out by 20 September.
* On 18 September, UK rider [wrote|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/441312742] to Bolt from a [new account|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/232980556/overview?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] (“*Account 2*”) claiming “_My account with Bolt is subject to a fraud and it’s been erased, so I need to recover it and claim money back_”. This was under the heading of ‘Personal Data Request’.
** Account 2 appears to have been created on 18 September.
** Unfortunately, CS wrote back confirming that their account was active (CS made a mistake and looked at the new account, not the old one). Rider clarified that they created a new account - unfortunately, CS responded “_once you erase your account, it cannot be retrieved_”.

* On 19 September, CS [confirmed|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/441312742] to the rider “_I have logged out of all devices linked to your account including the one you are currently using_”.
** It is unclear whether this concerns Account 1 or Account 2. I should check this.

Hello [~accountid:642aa587f8bc2116accacb6d],

The reason the invoice does not appear to be paid, is that *not all previous invoices have been paid in full*, and *any payment received always goes towards the oldest invoice*.

If we go to the [invoices|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/business-invoicing/businessCompanies/edit/194719?tab=invoices&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A50%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D] tab, for the company, there is a summary, where we can see the ‘Total expense’ minus the 'Total income:

!image-20241021-205301.png|width=100%,alt="image-20241021-205301.png"!



+*Calculation to see balance at end of the month*+

Total expense - Total income = Balance

*1,036,482.55* - *964,179* = 72,303.55 HUF 



If we compare this to what the value of the most recent invoice was:



+*Calculation to see outstanding amount at end of the month*+

Balance (from above) - Most recent invoice (Sep 2024) = Outstanding amount

72,303.55 - 72,303.04 = 0.51 HUF



If you compare the amount received in the ‘Income’ column, vs the amount due in the ‘Expense’ column for the previous month, you can see that more often than not, the amount differs, which is why the account is in arrears for 0.51 HUF and the most recent payment is not being reflected in the system as paid.

{code:sql}WITH data AS (

    FROM geo.rides_routing_eta_route
    WHERE created_hour >= DATE '2024-10-22'
      AND error_type IS NOT NULL
),
total AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_count
    FROM geo.rides_routing_eta_route
    WHERE created_hour >= DATE '2024-10-22'
)
SELECT
    cause,
    COUNT(*) AS count,

* *CXA solutions/suggestions:*
** Consider adding a note to the driver stories about where to take unclaimed packages
** Consider enabling paid wait time for Send orders only at the end of the ride.
* *T&C:*
** 1. If feasible and possible, the Driver will make reasonable efforts to contact the Client and bring the Package back to the Client or hand it over to the Recipient. 
** 2. *If the Client cannot be contacted*, the Driver will deliver the Package(s) to Bolt's designated office 
** 3. *If bringing the Package to Bolt's designated office is not feasible*, the Driver will deliver the Package(s) to the nearest police office and inform Bolt's customer support service accordingly. 
** If, while performing the aforementioned tasks, the Driver reasonably incurs additional costs that exceed the initially set price, the Driver is entitled to request a price review. Consequently, the Client acknowledges that an additional fee may be charged.
* *Alfred message:* If the recipient does not pick up the item, you can try to contact the recipient via the phone number provided by the sender. If you can’t reach them and the recipient does not show up *within 5 minutes*, you can leave the drop-off location and should *return the package* to the sender and inform the support team about the situation and location of the package.
** In the T&C, [FAQ|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/public/4404975872658], and in the Alfred message we mention 5 minutes of waiting. Current process has actions to ask the driver to wait more, but by the time driver contacts CS - CS responds back, way more than 5 minutes have passed (also, we don’t have live support, so agents might get to the ticket later). Agents should start solving the case *right away as the driver has waited enough*. 
* *CS process:*
** If the driver couldn’t deliver the parcel, they shouldn’t rely on CS for help. Instead, they should know how to resolve the issue quickly and efficiently themselves. So I want to avoid adding actions in the process where drivers must contact CS to resolve the issue (e.g. CS agent arranging the dropoff instead of rider/driver doing that themselves). 
** The logic of the process should be: driver couldn’t resolve the issue → contacted CS → received help → driver knows how to resolve the issue themselves in the future.

Dear Nurul*,* 

 

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *8 September 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order History (Pick-up and Drop-off)*

 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|smart-link] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,

 

Bolt

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer. 
You can ask the customer to reach out to their bank in order to confirm the authorized funds have been released. Their bank can locate the funds with the authorization date and amount.

User response to the {{package dependency change in MERGE_ONLY pipeline}} error must be modified to YES/NO response in [PullRequestCheckUserValidationStep|https://github.com/bolteu/backend-platform/blob/79279838df017786dc69f48137ec4442542c197c/builder/packages/backend/src/builder/service/steps/PullRequestCheckUserValidationStep.ts#L170]. User’s choice to continue the pipeline must be explicitly written in the log, so we could track it in case there’s a Builder incident and we need to investigate.

This chance will have a side-effect because now we’ll have 2 errors that are resumable: {{package dependency change}} and {{PR not reviewed}}. If both occur at the same time, only one error would be presented to the user (package dependency change) and the second one (PR not reviewed) not be hidden. User might ignore the first error (dependency change) without knowing that he also ignored the hidden one (PR not reviewed). This usability issue must be resolved in 2 ways:
1. Modify builder user-interactive messaging infrastructure to display independent messages, each with its own response. This would be the conceptually correct approach, but very expensive to implement for such a tiny gain that is achieved by this story. Think twice about doing it this way.
2. Aggregate all error messages into one single UI message and present the user with the most limiting user action. Might not look as nice as solution 1, but it’s much easier to implement, doesn’t mislead the user and solves the the issue. Strongly recommend to go for this option.

+*BACKGROUND*+

* Bolt Ops (Estonia) and AS Kindlustus (Estonia) entering into a collaboration agreement, to offer Bolt drivers discount on Casco insurance and Motor third-party liability insurance as part of the Bolt Rewards Program.
** AS responsible for issuing loyalty cards (which provide 10% discount to the two insurance providers), as instructed by Bolt.
** Bolt responsible for contacting drivers registered on the platform to “encourage” them to use the loyalty program, by giving out cards. Bolt share use app, blog and other internal comms to do so.
* The transaction value is 0 - Bolt does not incur any cost here.
* Agreement attaches a pre-prepared DSA, which appears to follow our standard form. 
** Lists Bolt as exporter of the following driver data: Name, personal ID number, phone number and email address.
** Purposes are to allow drivers to enroll in the loyalty program, to check whether the drivers have active Bolt status and for any other ‘incidental’ purposes.

Ah, apologies - the preliminary injunction is indeed not directed at us. It seems they added it as simply proof of a previous preliminary injunction that was successful for them (possibly to pressure us).

Their complaint does have some holes in it (such as the pictures not having timestamps, Romil checking and confirming that the NPZ works fine, etc.). Since it is still not certain that will actually go to court, we have some options (none of which are ideal).

# *Not do anything.* 
This would essentially mean to call their bluff. We have provided several explanations as to why this claim is unfounded and it _might_ be that they are simply pressuring us to pay the legal fees but won’t actually go to court. This is backed by the fact that they have given us over the course of a long period several “ultimatums” and “threats” that they will go to court if do not solve this by date xx.xx - however so far, they have not went to court. We therefore can have reason to believe that the statement in their latest letter that they are already putting together a claim is not actually true since they themselves do not believe this would be successful in court.

*RISK*: There is still a possibility that they are serious and will turn to court, and soon. The fact that they shared the previous preliminary injunction proves that they have went to court with such cases before and have been successful at least in getting the preliminary injunction - no info on if the court case in general has been in their favor or not.
Also, “not doing anything” would leave this matter hanging for an uncertain time and we would not be able mark it as solved.
Also, I would very much like to avoid an actual court case. While I believe our chances of winning the case are not low, we would likely need to hire an external counsel to represent us in court and their legal fees alone would exceed the claim in question.

# *Provide them another substantive response.* 
We could repeat that their claim is unfounded and also explain that the NPZ is accurate, their photos do not have timestamps and do not prove anything, if a scooter is left on the property without the user ending the ride then they should turn to the user and not Bolt. Furthermore, we could offer them an “agreement” that in the future, if any scooter should still end up on the property, we will react to their request of removing the scooter in 12-24 hours - just like pursuant to our agreement with the city of Bonn.

*RISK*: They may completely dismiss this and still turn to court. This is because so far they have dismissed all other responses from us. It is therefore possible this new response still has no effect (mainly because we still won’t pay the fees) and they will turn to court.

# *Alternatively, we arrange a call with the lawyer.* 
This might help in case there has been some sort of misunderstanding. We would explain the same key points as in point 2 and try to further explain to them that we have done everything that is technically possible and have had no issues with the city of Bonn with the same issues - therefore we do not see any reason to treat them differently than the city of Bonn. Furthermore, we should urge them to send these types of scooter removal request through our CS.

*RISK*: The result would be the same as sending them the written response, as in point 2 - they would dismiss our reasoning and still turn to court or continue to threaten us with turning to court.

# *Pay the fees as a sign of good faith / compromise.* 
Since the fees are relatively small, we could pay them but accompany this with a firm explanation that we do not agree with any of their claims and are making the payment as a compromise. We could even go as far a draft a compromise agreement where we agree to pay the fees and they agree to withdraw any and all demands relating to this subject matter and agree that if in the future they should find that another scooter is parked illegally on their property, then their first course of action is to submit a request to CS to have Bolt remove the scooter in 12-24 hours.

*RISK*: They would regard this an opportunity to send more claims our way in the future, since we agreed to pay the first one. They would regard it as their “victory” after a successful pressurizing and believe they can repeat it in the future. The only real way to combat this is to send them a counterclaim, based on their “extortion” (if it is indeed that) and warn them of going to court ourselves - this however seems excessive if the claims in questions are considerably small.

I’ll also discuss this some other GFT members, but please provide me your thoughts on the above options in the meantime.

After the standby test, Okai ran the dynamic tests. However, they did not find any abnormalities when it comes to current. The ECU already limits the maximum current to 17.5A, and they do not suggest further limiting it, when motors age (like our fleet 2 years old) they lose efficiency, so limiting the current will prevent vehicles from reaching full speed. Okai does not believe that adjusting the output current is related to solving this issue. Okai Engineers considered the data as inconclusive ("strange" in Okai’s words). The current was not stable and yielded different data in concurrent runs. Okai’s R&D team is talking to German engineers to redo the dynamic test.

Meanwhile, Bolt ran a live test with a few vehicles in Porto using a test FW provided by Okai. When analyzing the data, Okai found that the battery level abnormally jumps in dynamic processes, so they currently suspect it is related to the battery SOC reading and the motor state. They requested the BMS logs from the batteries involved in the test (complete conversations in Slack). We shipped the only BMS tool we still have at the HQ to Porto, and now we are waiting for LOPS will collect the batteries and extract the logs. 

Okai Germany Engineers went to Bolt’s Solingen Warehouse last Friday, where a few scooters were made available to their engineers for some dynamic tests and battery BMS log collection. Okai still has to present us with the results of this visit.

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer.

As we discussed on our call, here is the discussion points:

The process of launching the project when Bolt blocks customers or partners due to DPA reports (LER) is hindered by several key issues:

# *Local confidentiality requirements and police approval*: Sharing information about why someone is blocked is required by the privacy law. However, sharing this information can be prohibited due to the local confidentiality requirements or obligation to get the approval from the police. Such local market analysis requires a costly regulatory analysis which complicates the process.
# *No clear operational guide*: There’s no standardized procedure from local ops on handling these cases, leading to uncertainty in our analysis.
# *Privacy concerns*: Contacting victims or suspects can violate privacy laws and considered as an invasion in privacy and impede investigations for the police.
# *Outcome uncertainty*: Bolt’s decisions may differ from police findings, creating complications and delays for Bolt and raised concerns from customers and partners.
# *Driving team*: Managing these cases should be led by central safety team, not local operations to ensure we have standardised global process.

Here is the timeline of events:
1. A [PR|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/111976] was created in bolt-serer. It included a service rename (and, therefore, a new name and gen config file for the Redis). 
2. Config-less [picked it up|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/111976#issuecomment-2363104314] as a new Redis instance and generated a proxy-config PR to add a new Redis.
3. proxy-config PR was merged. A new Redis was created.
4. The original bolt-server PR was *closed*.
5. A new bolt-server PR was created. It also included the same rename of the service.
6. config-less did not pick it up again because the Redis with that name had already been created

The bug happened in step 2. The old Reddis was left “dangling” as nothing used it any more. Config-less should have generated a PR  which deletes the old Reddis and creates the new one.

Unblocking the driver would therefore be a business decision and depends on how high do you assess the risk that this is actually a case of impersonation and that it likely to re-occur and put the safety of riders (and Bolt’s reputation) at risk. Essentially, the question is whether based on our internal investigation we can say that the suspicion of fraudulent activity has been _disproven_ or not (see also clause [13.4 of the Driver T&Cs|https://bolt.eu/no-no/legal/tnc-drivers/?category=rides#:~:text=13.4.%20We%20may,disproves%20such%20suspicions.]).

If the risk is too high and not acceptable to you then the driver should remain blocked. In such a case the lawyer should be answered with the following points in mind:

* Taking into account the circumstances of the case, Bolt has reasonable grounds to believe that the photos taken by the users have been taken in the same vehicle. This comes from the following:
** there are two separate cases where users have complained about the driver not matching the profile picture of Tabish;
** the pictures in question display the interior of a car which is the same model that is registered under Tabish’s account; – {color:#ff5630}PLEASE CONFIRM THIS{color}
** the order ID’s under which the two users have submitted the complaints can be linked with orders that have been completed under Tabish’s account;

In this case we have not been able to disprove the suspicion of account-sharing and there exist circumstances that support that this was indeed account-sharing (or a case of a fake profile picture).
* Bolt takes the safety of its users and the integrity of the Bolt Platform very seriously. The prohibition of account sharing and the requirement of profile pictures serves this exact purpose (see also clause 3.8 of the Driver Terms and Conditions). Bolt strives to react to all potential fraud cases in a fair but proportional manner, taking into account both the rights of the drivers but also the safety of riders and the rights of Bolt.
* We have also taken into account the history of Tabish’s two separate cases of a failed selfie verification. In these cases Tabish was ultimately given the benefit of the doubt and, as a sign of good faith, the account was not suspended. However, since the user complaints are recurring cases of fraud suspicion, we cannot repeat the same benefit of the doubt.
* As in this case there a two separate occasions where users have expressed concerns of feeling un-safe, Bolt regards this issue with utmost importance. We assess that the risk of continuous fraudulent activity is too high for Bolt’s risk appetite. In order to ensure the safety of riders and the integrity of the Bolt Platform, we have therefore decided to not lift the suspension.

+*Notes*+: 

What I observed by analysing duplicated related requests is that most duplicate account issues occur when users attempt to create additional profiles. This typically happens because they are unable to reserve a car due to a *negative debt balance* on their primary profile, which prevents further bookings.

Since some *Ops and CS* teams don’t have access to view or address these balance issues, we (*Tech Support)* is responsible for checking the user’s profile balance to determine if this is the cause of the problem (I have requested the permission for our rental team and it has been given, [admin|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/transactions?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn])

Our process for handling these cases should be as follows:

# *Balance Check*: If a user’s profile or one of their profiles shows a negative debt balance, this is usually the reason they cannot reserve a car.
# *Error Message Analysis*: If the balance is not the issue, we should examine the error message:
#* If the message indicates *fraud-related* concerns, escalate to the *Fraud Team*.
#* If the issue appears to be related to *verification* or if we encounter an unfamiliar message, we should involve the *Verification Team*.
#* For any other issues outside these categories, escalate to the *Drive Development (Drive Devs)* team.

I believe this approach will ensure efficient handling and proper escalation based on the nature of each issue.

Any feedback or additional details is welcomed!

*Purpose of the doc*: 

* Define clear *escalation guidelines* for our team regarding Slack verification requests.
* Ensure alignment between *Drive Devs, Verification Devs*, and other stakeholders such as *Product Teams*, *Ops*, and *Customer Support*.
* Help us understand potential *hurdles* faced by verification specialists, CS and Ops and provide steps to resolve these issues quickly and accurately.

h4. *Drive Devs Escalation*

* *When to escalate*: Escalation to the Drive Devs should occur when the issues are:
** Not *_fraud or verification_* related

* *What to include*:
** Detailed log information from the session.
** Screenshots or recordings of the issue (if applicable).

h4. *Verification Devs Escalation*

* *When to escalate*: Escalation to the *Verification Devs* should occur in cases related to:
** *User profile issues* (e.g., duplicate accounts if not related to user balance, incorrect verification).
** Errors or delays in the *identity verification process* (e.g., failed ID checks).
** Issues with *document uploads* or *account approvals*.

* *What to include*:
** Detailed log information from the session.
** Screenshots or recordings of the issue (if applicable).

*Common users hurdles*:

* *Duplicate users*:

** *Problem*: 
*** Users may accidentally create duplicate accounts, causing confusion or failed verification attempts.
*** Users change their details such as phone number, email address, issues such as users being twins etc . 
*** And other legitimate issues that are not necessarily the user’s mistake.
** *Resolution*:
*** Ask CT tier 2 to revoke the driving license. 
*** The reporter should go to Ops or Verification depending on the issue. CS Tier 2 will be able to see the verification flow and identify the exact reason for the verification failure.
* *Payments & Carsharing booking issues*:

** *Problem*: Users may experience payment rejection or failure when booking vehicles.
** *Resolution*:
*** Basic troubleshooting with users (e.g., ensure payment method is up-to-date, clear cache).
*** If payment system glitches are suspected, escalate to the *Drive Devs* for investigation.

*Roles and Responsibilities:*


* *Tech Support Engineers*: Frontline responders to user issues in Slack *_#carsharing-support_*. We are responsible for basic troubleshooting and determining when escalation is needed.
* *Drive Devs*: Handle escalations related to vehicle functionality and trip/booking related bugs.
* *Verification Devs*: Manage escalations related to user accounts, verification, and identity checks.
* *Product Teams*: Collaborate with us (Tech Support) and developers to address larger scale issues impacting the user’s experience.
* *Ops Team*: Ensures smooth operations by monitoring escalations and providing resources for swift resolution.
* *Customer Support*: Assists in user communication and provides details, info and feedback from users that may inform future product updates.

*Escalation workflow*:

* A post regarding verification or duplicate profile in Slack and *Tech Support* encounters an issue.
* We *troubleshoot* or provide an immediate resolution if possible.
* If unresolved, escalate to either *Drive Devs* or *Verification Devs* following the guidelines above.
* Include *all necessary logs and screenshots* in the escalation ticket.
* Monitor the issue for a response and ensure timely communication back to the user.

** *a.*name, address, place of residence and postal address;
** *b.*date of birth and gender;
** *c.*administrative characteristics;
** *d.*in case of a legal person, instead of the data referred to under a and b: name, address, postal address, legal form and place of business.

** *b.*the identifying data claimed;

** *d.*the title of the claim.

* *5*In case of urgent necessity, a demand as referred to in the first paragraph may be made orally. In that case, the investigating officer shall subsequently put the claim in writing and provide it to the person to whom the claim is addressed within three days of the claim being made.

** *a.*the data referred to in subsection 4;
** *b.*the data provided;
** *c.*the offence and, if known, the name or otherwise as precise an indication as possible of the suspect;
** *d.*the facts or circumstances showing that the conditions referred to in the first paragraph have been met.

Hey [~accountid:5cd53b8f27454f0fe457a830] , thanks so much for the explanations - that’s very helpful!

*My comments / overview:*

* Even though these are vehicle documents (not directly about Driver B), they are still linked to Driver B’s profile. Reusing them just for convenience could be seen as unnecessary processing of Driver B’s data, and thus be very hard to argue in case of a complaint / regulatory investigation.
** Ideally, we should ask Driver A to provide their own documents to avoid unnecessary use of Driver B’s data. If reusing documents is essential, you need to make sure it's really necessary for the situation and not just for convenience.
* You didn’t mention whether Driver B has given permission to use their vehicle documents for someone else’s application. Without their consent, this could be a problem under GDPR.
** If these documents are connected to Driver B personally, we’ll likely need to get their consent before using them for Driver A’s application. 
* GDPR requires that any data we use is accurate and up-to-date. So, there’s a risk that Driver B’s documents might not be accurate when applied to Driver A’s situation, especially if the car’s ownership or details have changed.
** Is it possible for us to double-check that the information is still correct before reusing the documents to avoid any errors?
* Under GDPR, Driver B has rights regarding their personal data (as do other users), such as the right to know how it’s being used or the right to object. Driver B might not want their documents used for another driver’s application, even if it seems harmless.
* An extra layer of issues could arise in cases where Driver B owns the car and rents it out to Driver A, we need to be extra careful to make sure we’re handling the data properly, especially when car ownership is involved.
** Is there a way for us to check this?



Bottom line - I advise against proceeding with this initiative, unless we make sure we have a clear process that prevents us from being exposed to the problems I’ve laid out above.

This claim is in relation to a soiling incident by a passenger which took place on 4 October 2024, where the passenger vomited in the driver’s car. 
The amount the driver is claiming is £550. The breakdown is as below: 
Compensation - £140 
2 days earnings - £300
Cleaning cost - £60
Total - £500 + claim fee £50 = £550

The driver has already been paid £60 on 5th October as confirmed by [~accountid:5f17f7301084620015f4972a] below. 

The driver is unhappy that we wasn’t paid the journey fee. He drove only 100 yards in when the incident took place and the passenger left his car after which he ended the trip. 

*OPTIONS AVAILABLE TO BUSINESS:*

*Option 1: Accept Liability:* Bolt can accept liability and pay the amount claimed (£550) however, after reviewing the claim, breakdown of the amount includes cleaning fee which has already been reimbursed and the compensation and loss of earnings claimed is quite disproportionate.

*Option 2: Defend the claim:* Bolt can defend the claim as Bolt’s liability under the Terms is clearly limited and the primary defence lies in emphasising the exclusion clauses, particularly those related to loss of earnings and liability for passenger actions. However please not this will take time and resource from the legal team.

*Option 3: Settle the claim:* Bolt can make a counter offer to the driver as a goodwill gesture provided the driver withdraws the claim to settle this dispute outside of court. Please bear in mind that a partial offer may be rejected by the claimant.

My view is that the best way forward is to settle the claim by offering the driver a goodwill gesture of X amount without admitting liability, which is contingent upon the driver withdrawing the claim.

Hi, everybody! I am coming to you with an update on how we communicate with accused users in regards to safety incidents

*Context:*
We had some Safety Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), like the ones covering physical and sexual assault cases, where it was mentioned that we couldn’t share the allegation with the reported user. Together with CS Safety, Privacy and Legal teams, we have reviewed the guidelines for Eater and Courier Events to make them compliant, more clear, and to make investigations more meaningful.*Update:*
Please see the [Delivery Safety Case Handling Workflow|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/90194?country=global&language=en] and the example templates which are available in the [safety event-specific SOPs|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4408525302418123?country=global&language=en]. I’ve outlined the main points of the update below:

*Investigating the report*

* We should always inform the reported user about the suspension on their account;
* We should state that the report came from ‘a third party’, e.g ‘_we have received a report stating that’_ when reaching out to the reported user;
* We should not share the date of the event unless otherwise stated in the SOP, instead we should refer to a time period when the alleged behaviour occurred, e.g. ‘_in the month of July 2024’_;
* We should not share the allegation in detail, instead we should address the allegation by paraphrasing it in a professional manner, refraining from using slang or sharing excessive details. While it’s important to address the allegation, confidentiality must be maintained and specific information from the report cannot be shared, as that might endanger the reporting user, the police investigation and/or public safety.
* For safety incidents such as reports of rape, homicide, terrorism threat, abduction, illegal detainment, we should imply non-compliance with Terms and Conditions as the reason for suspending the accused user’s account for the duration of the internal investigation.

* _After 24h when the immediate threat has passed, we may share the allegation in a paraphrased manner._

*Communicating the consequential action*

* When we consequently suspend a courier, we must notify them of the suspension/termination and the allegation via email too;
* When we suspend a fleet courier, we must notify the fleet owner via email simultaneously:

* This applies to both *investigative* and *consequential* suspensions. _This does not apply to when we consequently, after concluding the investigation, warn a courier;_
* We must also specify which fleet they are in association with and specify the date from which they are suspended/terminated.

* We must include references to T&C’s wording;
* Lastly, we must include a link where the courier can appeal our decision, if we have suspended their account or terminated the partnership with them.

If you notice anything is off or you have questions/concerns regarding the changes, please send me a ticket via [Risk service desk|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/36/group/1250/create/2094]. Thank you!

While testing the feature branch update scenarios, it was discovered that:

* The first step {{Validating feature branch}} already verifies the feature branch HEAD
* {{Protecting feature branch}} happens only 5-15 seconds after {{Validating feature branch}}
* Feature branches are only refreshed (pulled) [once a minute|https://github.com/bolteu/backend-platform/blob/master/builder/packages/backend/src/builder/config/config.defaults.production.ts#L167]

This yields to the following facts:

* The unverified branch update can only technically happen during a very small pipeline timeframe (5-15s),
the rest pipeline duration is safe thanks to the branch protection
* An additional verification step would not catch all those updates, because the branch is likely not to be pulled during that small timeframe

As an extra validation step would not solve the small remaining problem fully, there is no point in implementing it.
Branch protection already solves the problem for 99%.

Dear Adrian*,* 



*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *16 September 2024.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.



We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order History* 



For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/privacy/|smart-link] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.





Yours sincerely,



Bolt

HI [~accountid:5d91ad8a1d47a50c34d48412] 

On a general note, although couriers are not hired directly by Bolt in PT, but by the fleets instead, one can claim that fleets render a service to Bolt through the couriers, and *Bolt could be held jointly responsible for the breach of labour related requirements*. Hence, I strongly recommend the project to move into MVRA and onboarding processes, implementation of controls to be review by relevant support teams including by GFT again. We can re-open this ticket at that time. 

Please see below answers to your questions:

+*Minimum age:*+ *From what age could we start onboarding couriers in Portugal?*

For the purpose of this analysis, we assume that couriers are hired by fleets, and not by Bolt directly. Generally Bolt could start onboarding couriers when they reached the age of 16 years old. 

 +Minors+ +*hired as employees*+ +of the fleets:+

 A minor that has *reached the age of 16* can be employed provided:

* They have completed compulsory schooling or are enrolled and attending secondary school OR attending a form of education or training that confers, as the case may be, compulsory schooling, a professional qualification, or both.
* They have the physical and mental capacities appropriate to the job.

A minor that is *under the age of 16* can be employed provided:

* they have completed compulsory schooling or are enrolled and attending secondary level education and
* the work is light (meaning simple, defined tasks which, because of their nature, the physical or mental effort required or the specific conditions in which they are carried out, are not likely to harm their physical integrity, safety and health, school attendance, participation in guidance or training programmes, ability to benefit from the instruction given, or their physical, mental, moral, intellectual and cultural development) – which we assume is the case for couriers, given the effort required.

 +Minors+ +*hired as independent contractors*+ +of the fleets:+

 Minors can be onboarded as independent contractors:

# If they are at least 16 years old; or
# In case they are younger than 16 years old, if they have completed compulsory schooling or are enrolled and attending secondary school.

+Minors+ +*hired as employees*+ +of the fleets:+

 The work of minors is subject to various limitations and there is a set of duties imposed on the employer, of which the following stand out:

* A minor's normal working hours may not exceed 8 hours per day and 40 hours per week. In the case of light work carried out by minors under the age of 16, the normal working hours may not exceed 7 hours per day and 35 hours per week.
* Minors are exempt from working under the adaptability regime, bank of hours or concentrated hours when this could jeopardise their health or safety at work.
* As a rule, minors may not perform overtime.
* As a rule, minors may not perform night work.
* The daily work period of minors must be interrupted by an interval lasting between 1 and 2 hours, so that they do not work more than 4 hours consecutively if they are under 16 years of age, or 4h30 if they are 16 years of age or over.
* Minors have the right to a daily rest period between work periods of two consecutive days, lasting for a minimum of 14 consecutive hours if they are under 16 years of age, or 12 consecutive hours if they are 16 years of age or older.
* Minors' weekly rest period lasts two days, consecutive, if possible, in each seven-day period.

+Minors+ +*hired as independent contractors*+ +of the fleets:+

 Minors who carry out activities independently are subject to the limitations established for employment contracts with minors.

Regarding the second set of questions:

{quote}when a case starts as a safety issue but later turns into a customer service matter, should the ticket be closed as a safety case? And what is the proper procedure regarding tags in this situation—should we remove the safety tags and add only the customer service tags, or should the safety tags remain?{quote}

It depends on whether the case was reported as safety but turned out to be a fully non-safety issue or a combination of safety and non-safety:

* If the case starts as safety but turns into a non-safety issue only, then the case should be closed as non-safety (Tier: Tier 1; Severity: None + the applicable non-safety issue tags)
* If the case is a combination of safety and non-safety, then it depends on whether the safety agent is trained to handle the non-safety issue. 
** If yes, the agent handles the safety part first, setting the *Tier* as *Safety*, setting the applicable severity level and adding the relevant safety issue tags, and then handles the non-safety issue and adds the applicable non-safety issue tags but does not change the tier or the severity level.
** If no, the safety agent handles the safety part, sets the applicable severity level, adds the relevant safety issue tags, and then escalates the case to *Tier 1*, where the agent will resolve the non-safety issue and add the applicable non-safety issue tags. *The safety tags and severity should not be changed or removed.* 

All this is covered in all of the vertical safety case handling workflows.

Hey [~accountid:712020:88fb6bce-439f-4d0c-a864-dbb299763f36] 
Sorry for the late response. 

At fraud, our metrics and actions are based on the driver profile, not the partner. What we have seen in the PT market is a lot of cases where drivers delete their account or even jump fleet and for us that cleans the slate and we see the new driver id as a clean driver. 
We have a driver reporting sheet with the local market, because due to regulation we have to do the blocks manually there. It can be seen that one partner has multiple accounts coming back to continue their fraud. 
If the enrolment process is strong and it can accommodate the duplication check (like in UK for example where returning driver that is removed from the platform is almost impossible) then these repeating offender will not come back. 
Even if fraud switches their metrics on partner level, it will take 2,3 driver profiles worth of fraud to see the partner level spike and report it and then even when that gets blocked if he can come back and create a new one, the work would be in vain.
If there is no check on the re-enrolment on partner level and we allow signups again, a single real person can have multiple partners (which the locals do not see) and each of those partners have multiple driver profiles (which hides the fraud from us to see as well) then this flow lets them abuse us on both scenarios. 
Maybe an improvement on the enrolment and duplication check can solve the core issue and lower the fraud later along the funnel

Hey [~accountid:5d91ad8a1d47a50c34d48412], I received the finalised advice from the external counsel on this and the answers are below. Please check and let me know if you have any further questions.

----

# Minimum age: From what age can we start onboarding couriers in Azerbaijan?

_Generally, minors can enter into employment agreements (relevant for the fleet couriers) from 15 years old, and register as individual entrepreneurs (relevant for the individual couriers) from 16 years old. Therefore, depending on the type of our cooperation with such couriers, it is either 15 or 16 years old._

# Documentation: Are there any additional documents required (e.g., parental consent, specific work permits) during the onboarding process?

_For the_ *_fleet couriers_*_:_ 

# _Employment agreement with the relevant fleet;_
# _Parental consent (from both parents/guardians) for entering into such employment agreement;_
# _Separate parental consent (from both parents/guardians) for entering into an agreement with Bolt (i.e. accepting our Courier T&Cs.)_ 

_At the same time, only the fleet-employer is responsible for the compliance with all relevant labour laws and regulations. Therefore, if the agreement between Bolt and the fleet indicates that the fleet has to ensure such compliance, we can skip documents No 1 and 2 and request only document No. 3._

_For the_ *_individual couriers_*_:_

# _Tax certificate confirming they registered as an individual entrepreneur;_
# _Parental consent (from both parents/guardians) for entering into an agreement with Bolt (i.e. accepting our Courier T&Cs.)_ 

_For both cases above, no requirements exist as to the form or the content of such parental consent. Therefore, we could request simple written consent signed by both parents._

# Other requirements: Any further legal considerations or restrictions we should be aware of?

_For the fleet couriers, there are specific employment law restrictions re the working hours, delivery of specific goods, etc. (please see section 3 in the document below.). While we are not obliged to monitor this as we are not the employer, it would still be good to keep all of these requirements in mind and try to follow them._

_The respective legal advice is here -_ [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1o6sltISp5iYloid1m4uTiZ3dq0zJq4CD/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1o6sltISp5iYloid1m4uTiZ3dq0zJq4CD/edit|smart-link]

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *1 October 2024.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.



We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Balance Reports*

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.





Yours sincerely,



Bolt

As agreed, here is the short summary from our call:

* You have responded to my questions in[ this document|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/5472583743/Privacy+review]
* The project itself does not raise any risk or concerns, except the part below
* As agreed, let’s come up with the ideas on how to eliminate the risk related to recycled phone number issue and phoneless account:
** Issue: Your proposal in the RFC states that when a user signs up via the social account and later on enters the phone number for completing the order, we detect the duplicate account in our system. When the phone number from a new account matches the one from an old account, you propose to log in the user to the old account and archive the new account.
*** As we discussed, this raises concerns as some users can get access to the old account that is in fact not their account and previous phone number owner did not update their phone number.
*** We discussed that we should not let users to log in to the old account if their phone numbers match as there is a risk of unauthorised access to the account.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Proposed solutions we discussed*
{panel}

* *Short-term (to not block the project)*
** *Medium risk for privacy:* when a user enters a phone number to the account registered with the social token, we do not let this user to log in to the duplicate account if the phone number matches the existing account. Instead, we archive the old account and let the user use their new account.
*** In this case, we prevent unauthorised access to the existing account.
*** If the account owner contacts us and ask to reactivate the account, we advise to create a new account with the up-to-date phone number.
*** While it’s not perfect for the privacy compliance when we do not allow users to proceed using their account, we balance the risk against the unauthorised access where we still will archive the account and ask both users to register new ones.
*** However, if we see the spike in user’s complaints, we may need to develop the long-term solution quicker.
* *Long-term solution*
** *Low risk for privacy:* when a user enters a phone number to the account registered with the social token, we do not let this user to log in to the duplicate account if the phone number matches the existing account. Instead, we archive the old account and send an immediate notification to the account owner, informing that they need to update their phone number. 
** After the user contacts CS or logs in to the app, we have to come up with how we will allow the user to update their phone number, send an OTP, confirm it and reactivate the account. 
** Updating phone number can be done manually by the CS, but we have to automate it and allow the user to do it on their own, enter the phone number, confirm the OTP and reactivate the account automatically.

This long-term solution is better for the privacy compliance as we prevent an unauthorised access to the account and allow the old account owner to proceed using the account.

However, we need some additional resources to develop this solution.



Let me know your thoughts about the solutions.

Thank you for escalating to Customer Payments team. The customers don't always have a great visibility when the pre-authorization has been returned to them. Returning the pre-authorization is not something Bolt has much control over. 
Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

Please leave a comment on the ticket if you still want it to be escalated to the Customer Payments team. Else the ticket will be closed in 5 days.

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *22 August 2024.*

*Please be advised that the data you requested is not considered to be personal data. Nevertheless, Bolt is committed to cooperating with its customers and has fulfilled your request.*

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order History (Estimated Time and Distance)*

 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|smart-link] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;

* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,

 

Bolt

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer.

Hi [~accountid:5b7bea09d08e47445d6fd01e] below my thoughts regarding duration of blocks:

* This analysis will be based on the assumption the time limitations refer to driver account blocks (not fleet or riders).
* Blocks include mainly:
** *Suspensions (for breach of platform terms):* any temporary / fixed restriction of access from the platform including ‘precautionary suspensions’ (i.e. investigations).
** *Terminations (for breach of platform terms):* permanent blocks from the platform effective immediately.
* In Portugal we have 3 types of account blocks: compliance, fraud and safety.
* +Compliance blocks+:
** “14(2) - The operator of the electronic platform must block access to the services provided by the platform by … drivers … that fail to comply with any of the requirements referred to in this law”
** In general these blocks should last until compliance is re-established. This is easy to apply when we refer to a lack of document, but less clear if the lack of compliance relates to the illegitimate refusal of the service. 
* +Fraud and safety blocks+:
** TVDE law does not cover these situations
** At Global level the time period of blocks has not been entirely defined. [~accountid:62722e092db308007024a425] (thank you!!) kindly shared the main guiding principles:
*** When it comes to hard blocks it is up to the business when and if to unblock drivers based on the blocking reason: 
*** the general guidance on duration of the blocks is *to chose the shortest time period that gives effect to the commercial aim / need*. 
*** When it comes to fraud and safety blocks this significantly depends on the incident and fraud reason if and when to unblock (for instance, we may not want someone who raped a passenger any soon on the platform but if it is a case of speeding probably not the same).
** Blocking is a reclassification requirement in Portugal: “The digital platform exercises labour powers over the activity provider, including *disciplinary power, including exclusion from future activities on the platform by deactivating the account*” It can be argued that when suspending or terminating access to driver accounts, Bolt may be exercising disciplinary powers. Limiting fraud and safety blocks to certain periods IMO does not change the level of the reclassification risks. 
** It is important to counterbalance other elements too:
*** In Portugal the right to work is a constitutional right 
*** TVDE drivers can only exercise their work by registering themselves in an electronic platform according to TVDE law
*** TVDE law determines the requirements to become a TVDE driver in PT
*** Not establishing time limits to blocks could be seen as well as an abuse of law IMO.
* *As a summary:*
** There are no direct legal imposition regarding the duration of hard blocks. 
** Indirectly from the TVDE law we can understand that compliance blocks should be be imposed until compliance is restablished.
** Blocks can be permanent, but they should be justifiable to ensure mitigation of risk regarding abuse of law. 
** The general guidance on duration of the blocks is to chose the shortest time period that gives effect to the commercial aim / need. 
* As a suggestion for next step I suggest that you contact [@aba.koita|https://taxify.slack.com/team/UC32P5XQC] (with [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] cc’d) since in FR there is already a list of time lines or duration for blocks. Alignment can be useful. Additionally, I suggest that you share again with legal when you have blocking process with duration in paper for another review having in mind the specific changes or improvements that LOPS wishes to deploy.

Thank you.
